newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks fall back below 5,000 points.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks fall back below 5,000 points.

text.p: Mexican stocks extended an initial slide at mid-morning trade on Friday to return to below the pyschological 5,000-point barrier, which they had cracked for the first time ever on Thursday.
Dealers said many investors had opted to take considerable profits chalked up in recent sessions on cue from a sharp fall in the Dow Jones and a surge in U.S. long bond yields.
The leading IPC share index was down 74.40 points, or 1.47 percent, at 4,993.43.
Trading volume .TV.MX of 74.8 million shares was still slow as it included a cross trade of 47.5 million shares in communications firm Iusacel.

Dealers said blue chips were down almost across the board on profit-taking, most notably on market heavyweights Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) and Bancomer, and on Kimberly-Clark de Mexico, which had gained strongly during the prior session.
On the broad market, decliners outnumbered gainers by 48 to 17 out of 78 stocks that had changed hands.
